question_text: The graph alongside shows the percentage $P$ of radioactive Carbon-14 remaining in an organism $t$ thousands of years after it dies.

subparts.stem: Use the graph to estimate the percentage of Carbon-14 remaining after 4000 years.
subparts.solution: When $t = 4$, $P \approx 60$. Therefore, there is about $60\%$ of Carbon-14 remaining after 4000 years.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Extract information directly from the given graph of $P$ against $t$.
step_by_step: Locate $t = 4$ on the horizontal axis (representing thousands of years).
Move vertically to meet the curve.
Read corresponding value on the vertical axis: $P \approx 60\%$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Misreading the scale of the axes.

subparts.stem: Use the graph to estimate the number of years for the percentage of Carbon-14 to fall to 50%.
subparts.solution: When $P = 50$, $t \approx 5.5$. Therefore, it will take approximately 5500 years for the percentage of Carbon-14 to fall to $50\%$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Find the independent variable corresponding to a given percentage on the graph.
step_by_step: Move horizontally to meet the curve.
Read the $t$-value: $t \approx 5.5$ thousand years, which is 5500 years.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to multiply $t$ by 1000 to express in years.

subparts.stem:
The equation of the graph is $P = 100 \times (1.1318)^{-t},\; t \ge 0$.
Calculate the percentage of Carbon-14 remaining after 8000 years.
subparts.solution: When $t = 8$, $P = 100 \times (1.1318)^{-8} \approx 37.1$. Therefore, there is about $37.1\%$ of Carbon-14 remaining after 8000 years.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Substitute the value of $t$ (in thousands of years) into the formula.

subparts.stem:
The equation of the graph is $P = 100 \times (1.1318)^{-t},\; t \ge 0$.
How long will it take for the percentage to fall to 15%?
subparts.solution: When $P = 15$, $15 = 100 \times (1.1318)^{-t} \implies t \approx 15.3$ \{using technology\}. Therefore, it will take approximately 15300 years for the percentage of Carbon-14 to fall to $15\%$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Solve an exponential equation using graphing technology or logarithms.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Leaving the final answer as 15.3 without converting from thousands of years to years.
